- Additional Insured: Please add AcmeCloud and its affiliates as additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis for liability arising out of Redwood's work.
- Waiver of subrogation: Waive subrogation for general liability and workers' comp to the extent allowed by law.
- Coverage minimums: GL $2M per occurrence / $4M aggregate; Cyber $2M; E&O $1M.
- Retroactive date: align policy retroactive date with contract effective date.
- Certificate: need COI and endorsement naming AcmeCloud; certificates delivered within 7 business days of counter-signature.

I've attached a marked-up summary of the redlines (Acme_MSA_highlights.pdf). Oliver from our broker is cc'd on this thread — he'll coordinate with his carrier. Please let me know if any of these are a blocker from Redwood's side or if you want to propose alternative language.

Mateo — thanks for the ping and the redlines. Quick triage below.

Summary position (recommended):
- Additional Insured: Accept in form but limit to "additional insured for liability arising out of the performance of the services" and only to the extent allowed by the primary policy. We should avoid blanket blanket additional insured umbrella exposure. Use an ISO endorsement reference where possible; see proposed wording below.
- Primary & Non-Contributory: We can accept "primary and non-contributory" provided insurer endorsement is obtained. Add conditional language: "to the extent permitted by carrier" and require endorsement from broker/insurer.
- Waiver of Subrogation: We will accept waiver of subrogation for GL and workers' comp where permitted by law and where insurer confirms in writing. For Cyber and E&O, we require insurer confirmation; many carriers will not waive subrogation for cyber without material underwriting.
- Retroactive Date: We cannot unilaterally change historical retro dates. If Acme requires retroactive date aligned to effective date, we can propose a compromise: accept a retroactive date no later than the contract effective date only if carrier will confirm in writing and there is no materially adverse premium or underwriting restriction. This will likely be rejected by the carrier without additional premium.
- Limits: The GL/Cyber/E&O numbers requested are higher than our standard for this tier. Propose we accept GL $2M/$4M and E&O $1M (if customer insists on Cyber $2M, require carrier confirmation and note potential pricing impact).

Proposed contract language (brief):
"Contractor shall name Customer (and its officers, directors and affiliates) as additional insured with respect to claims arising out of Contractor's operations performed under this Agreement. Such coverage shall be primary and non-contributory to the extent reasonably available and subject to the insurer's underwriting approval; Contractor shall provide an endorsement evidencing the same."

Operational asks for procurement/broker:
- Oliver: please confirm whether insurer can issue an additional insured endorsement and a waiver of subrogation for GL and WC, and whether the requested retroactive date/ CYBER retro is feasible without premium or underwriting exceptions. We need an endorsement sample (PDF) and a COI showing wording.
- Marissa: please hold on final countersign until Oliver provides endorsement PDF and COI. If carrier cannot endorse, we'll propose fallback language limiting additional insured scope.

I've attached a sample endorsement we prefer (Proposed_Endorsement_Sample.pdf). If Oliver can confirm, we can accept and instruct contracts to update the order form provision with the language above.

— Irene

Thanks for looping me in. Quick update from the broker side:

- Carrier: primary GL carrier is prepared to issue an Additional Insured endorsement and to endorse primary & non-contributory language, subject to insurer sign-off. I will request a draft endorsement — likely follows the CG 20 10/11-like language but we will provide the carrier-specific form.
- Waiver of Subrogation: GL and WC waiver is typically doable; cyber waiver is carrier-dependent and often declined without extra premium.
- Retroactive Date: aligning retro date to the contract effective date is not standard; carriers typically keep the original retro date. If Acme requires it, expect underwriter review and potential premium.
- Limits: We can provide COI showing the requested limits; however, moving to higher limits may require an endorsement/policy change.

Next steps from me: I will request endorsement sample and written confirmation on waiver feasibility and retroactive acceptance, and target delivery within 3 business days. Please confirm the precise naming for the Additional Insured that Acme wants on the endorsement ("AcmeCloud, Inc.", or "AcmeCloud, Inc. and its affiliates").
